title: The Chowchilla Bus Kidnapping
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the 1976 Chowchilla school bus kidnapping in California: summer-school bus driver Ed Ray and 26 children were hijacked, buried for about 12 hours in a moving van trailer at a Livermore rock quarry, and escaped by prying open the roof (Mike Marshall reportedly led the effort). The kidnappers, Fred Woods, James Schoenfeld and Richard Schoenfeld, were caught within about two weeks; the brothers were paroled after decades, while Woods was denied parole repeatedly. The episode also covers the victims' lasting trauma, the town's response, the Lifetime movie, and a Robert Goulet song. Episode closes with listener mail about racially biased traffic ticketing and traffic cameras in Chicago.
topics: Robert Goulet Ballad of Chowchilla Ray

segments.title: Opening banter and Jeopardy announcement
segments.summary: Josh announces the hosts' Jeopardy category appearance, then the hosts banter about the Chowchilla kidnapping and a listener tip, and Chuck's aunt's memories of the case.

segments.title: The hijacking and eleven-hour drive
segments.summary: Ed Ray's school bus with 26 children is hijacked after a white van blocks Avenue 1; Mike Marshall had gotten on the bus. The children are moved to vans, which are driven for eleven hours with no food, water or bathroom breaks.

segments.title: Burial in the Livermore quarry
segments.summary: The kidnappers bury a moving van trailer at a Livermore rock quarry, put the children and Ed Ray inside with some supplies, a ventilation system, and mattresses, and take names and contact information written on a Jack in the Box wrapper.

segments.title: Town response, FBI and media frenzy
segments.summary: The bus is found hidden under camouflage, and the FBI and state agencies descend on Chowchilla amid national media attention. Families gather at the firehouse; the search produces many dead ends.

segments.title: Escape from the trailer
segments.summary: The children escape after roughly 12 hours underground. Mike Marshall reportedly led the charge and Ed Ray helped pry open the hatch with wood from box springs; the group emerges at the quarry and a security guard calls authorities. The hosts discuss the danger of the roof caving in.

segments.title: Aftermath, Greyhound ride, Disneyland, and the Goulet song
segments.summary: The children return home by Greyhound bus and the town is celebrated with parades and a Disneyland trip. Ed Ray appears on Hollywood Squares. The hosts discuss Robert Goulet's song Ballad of Chowchilla Ray and the Air Supply tangent.
topics: Robert Goulet Ballad of Chowchilla Ray

segments.title: Kidnappers' backgrounds and motives
segments.summary: Fred Woods came from a wealthy California family; James and Richard Schoenfeld were less wealthy and had financial pressure from a housing deal loss. They planned the crime around the state budget surplus, expecting the state's insurance to pay the ransom, and they had written plans with misspellings.

segments.title: Capture, sentencing, parole and victims' trauma
segments.summary: The brothers and Woods were arrested within about two weeks; Richard confessed and Woods was caught in Vancouver. The court's bodily harm ruling was reversed, making them parole-eligible. Richard and James were paroled, Woods was repeatedly denied, and the victims continue to suffer trauma. Lifetime movie and Vox article are mentioned.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: Listener Valerie Mates writes about racially biased traffic ticketing, explaining that neighborhood road design, not only police bias, may drive ticket disparities seen with Chicago traffic cameras. The hosts close the episode.
